name: Guyana
summary_text: Guyana is dangerous for trans visitors — one of only five Western-Hemisphere countries still criminalising same-sex conduct (buggery carries life imprisonment on paper, though rarely enforced). The IACHR heard evidence in November 2024 of severe violence against trans women: 69 cases of violence against trans women documented 2018–2022, in a country of under a million people. Police fail to investigate anti-LGBT violence; there is no anti-discrimination legislation (the UN Human Rights Committee called for it in April 2024) and no legal gender recognition. Cross-dressing was decriminalised after a 2018 CCJ ruling (McEwan v AG), removing the most direct trans-expression statute, but the climate and investigative failure keep risk high. Georgetown has a small organised community (SASOD).

sources.title: Guyana | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): Guyana is one of only five Western Hemisphere countries still criminalising consensual same-sex conduct - Sections 352-354 of the Criminal Law Act ('gross indecency', attempted buggery, buggery with life imprisonment). Rarely enforced but fuels stigma. In 2025 five of six election-contesting parties, including the ruling party, supported decriminalisation. Cross-dressing was criminalised until 2018 (Section 153(1)(xlvii)), targeting trans people; no legal gender recognition.
IACHR hearing record (191st Period of Sessions): civil-society hearing on Guyana concerning LGBTI rights and gender-based violence - part of the Inter-American Commission's LGBTI rapporteurship work.

sources.title: Inter-American human rights body calls for urgent action on gender-based violence here - Stabroek News
sources.claim_summary: Stabroek News (Nov 2024): at an IACHR hearing requested by a local group, testimonies on gender-based violence in Guyana were heard; the Inter-American Commission called on Guyana to take urgent action.

sources.title: Guyana's transgender activists fight archaic law - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: BBC News (March 2017): Guyana's transgender activists fight the 1893 colonial-era cross-dressing law (Summary Jurisdiction Act, s.153(1)(XLVII)); trans woman Petronella Trotman was stabbed and attacked with bottles, then told by the magistrate to 'dress like a man' - 'We live in a very homophobic society.'

sources.title: CCJ rules in favour of Guyanese transgender women - Stabroek News
sources.claim_summary: Stabroek News (Nov 2018): the Caribbean Court of Justice ruled in favour of Guyanese transgender women (Quincy McEwan, Angel Clarke, Peaches Fraser et al.) - the cross-dressing law is unconstitutionally vague and violates freedom of expression; Section 153(1)(XLVII) struck from the laws of Guyana.

sources.title: Transgender activists in Guyana are fighting against archaic laws | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (March 2017): transgender activists in Guyana fight archaic transphobic laws - Trotman's scissors attack, the magistrate ordering her to 'dress like a man', and the 124-year-old cross-dressing law blocking justice.

sources.title: Police uses discriminatory laws to extort LGBT persons- SASOD - News Room Guyana
sources.claim_summary: News Room Guyana (May 2019): SASOD's Joel Simpson documents police using discriminatory laws to extort LGBT persons - men in 'compromising positions' threatened with arrest to extract bribes; those who do report face further discrimination at police stations.
